thread.title: Intel, Amazon and Tesla lead tech stocks lower on the first trading day of April

author: Philip van Doorn
title: Intel, Amazon and Tesla lead tech stocks lower on the first trading day of April
text:
Intel, Amazon and Tesla led big technology stocks lower Monday amid a broad decline for the U.S. market.
Chip maker Intel INTC, -6.07% tumbled 6.1% after China announced tariffs on over 100 U.S. product categories and Bloomberg reported that Apple Inc. AAPL, -0.66% will begin outfitting its Mac personal computers with its own chips in two years. According to Intel’s most recent annual report, 24% of its annual sales were to customers in China , including Hong Kong.
Don’t miss: Apple, Nike and 18 other U.S. companies have $158 billion at stake in China trade war
Amazon.com’s AMZN, -5.21% shares slid 5.2% after President Trump continued a tweetstorm against the internet retailer.
Trump bashed Amazon over its apparently sweet deal with the U.S. Post Office, which he said has been “causing a tremendous loss to the U.S.” Maybe the president will redirect some ire at the Post Office itself, which set the delivery prices Amazon is paying.
The Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, -2.74% viewed as a technology bellwether, dropped 2.7%, while the S&P 500 SPX, -2.23% was down 2.2%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -1.90% dipped 1.9%.

Among investors (at least), CEO Elon Musk’s twitter jokes about a fictional bankruptcy for the electric-car maker didn’t go over well . It’s possible that long-term shareholders have become less comfortable with the prospect of continual dilution of their ownership stakes in the company.
Tesla has $230 million in convertible bonds due in 2018 and $920 million in March 2019. It seems obvious that rather than refinance that debt, it will be converted to common shares. Tesla’s average quarterly share count was up 8.6% in the fourth quarter from a year earlier. If we go to the fourth quarter of 2016, the count was up 18.2% from the fourth quarter of 2015.
And after that conversion and dilution, Tesla will still need to raise cash, which, considering its recent downgrade by Moody’s Investor Service further into junk territory , likely means another sale of new shares. And further dilution.
